Pi Durable on an Android phone
The @badlogicgames experiment, collected and explained

Built 19 Oct 2026 for Kacper. Sources: 28 public X posts by Mario Zechner (@badlogicgames, creator of Pi), one replication post by @arisonxdaniel, the official Pi Durable announcement (earendil.com) and the Pi repo docs (github.com/earendil-works/pi). Times are Berlin time (UTC+2).

TL;DRWhat he didTimelinePrerequisitesReplicatePitfallsLinks
Before you start: Mario did not publish his phone app. He calls it "not a product, but a pi durable demo", said "decided to not publish this. it's a slop", and later "it's not in a good state". So you can't just install it. What you can do is retrace his path with the public pieces (Termux, the Pi CLI, the Pi Durable library) and have your own agent build the app, which is exactly what he did.

TL;DR

  • 2 Oct: he noticed the normal Pi coding agent runs inside Termux on Android.
  • 3–5 Oct: over a weekend he built "pim" ("pi mobile"), a personal chat/coding agent app on top of Pi Durable. He built it on the phone, using Pi itself. It has subagents, multiplayer, artifacts, a file browser and a git viewer, and it can switch execution to his Hetzner server.
  • 4 Oct: he moved from Termux to a bespoke native Android app that contains only the Termux parts he needs.
  • Since then: it has been his daily driver for all his work. He hasn't opened his laptop in days, and he has rewritten the app twice, also on the phone. Everything except the LLM calls runs on the phone (a non-rooted Pixel 11, a few hundred MB of RAM).

What he did and why (plain language)

Pi is a minimal coding agent that runs in a terminal. Pi Durable is a TypeScript library that Earendil released with Pi 1.0 on 1 Oct 2026. It provides the "harness" for an agent: it stores every conversation (in SQLite, for example), checkpoints every step so nothing is lost when the process dies, runs many conversations and subagents in parallel, and lets several clients (phone, tablet, browser) watch and steer the same agent.

The phone's job: the "brain" (the agent loop, the storage and a small server with a UI) runs on Android. Only the calls to the model (OpenAI, Anthropic and so on) go to the cloud. The agent's "hands", meaning the execution environment where bash and file edits run, can be the phone itself or a remote machine such as a Hetzner VPS. He can switch between them mid-session.

Why: in his words, "my phone is always with me and quite powerful", "don't need to dick around with a vpn", and "phone is just a nice way to ensure it's efficient enough during dev". He also says mobile "was not my motivation for durable. just a side effect". The phone was a stress test for the library.

Layers: Termux (a Linux userland on Android) → Node.js → Pi Durable harness + SQLite → his control plane and web UI (written by the agent) → any device that can reach the phone (his Android tablet, a browser).

Prerequisites

  • An Android phone with decent RAM. His is a Pixel 11, not rooted.
  • Termux from GitHub or F-Droid, not the deprecated Google Play build DOC. Optionally also Termux:API.
  • Node.js 22.19 or newer (Pi's requirement) DOC, plus git.
  • An LLM provider: a subscription or API key that you connect with /login in Pi DOC.
  • Optional: a VPS (like his Hetzner) for remote execution, and a second device such as a tablet or laptop browser as a client.
  • For the native-app stage only: an Android build toolchain, or an agent that can drive one. INFERRED

Step-by-step replication

FROM HIS POSTS means Mario said it. DOC means the official Pi or Earendil docs. INFERRED means my reconstruction of a gap he didn't explain; verify these steps yourself.

Stage 1: Pi in Termux DOCFROM HIS POSTS

This is where he started on 2 Oct ("pi works in termux on Android … still does!"). These commands come from packages/coding-agent/docs/termux.md:

pkg update && pkg upgrade
pkg install nodejs git
npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
pi --version
mkdir -p ~/work && cd ~/work
pi            # then type /login inside pi to connect a model

Optional extras from the docs:

termux-setup-storage        # access /storage/emulated/0
pkg install termux-api      # clipboard via termux-clipboard-get/set (needs the Termux:API app too)

The docs also suggest adding a ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md that tells Pi it is running in Termux, for example "Open URLs with termux-open-url".

Stage 2: Get Pi Durable and its examples on the phone DOC

The Earendil post says: "Point your agent at packages/durable in a Pi checkout, have it read the README, the over thirty examples, the small coding agent on Pi Durable…". In the current repo the examples live in packages/durable/test/examples/ (00-conversation.ts … 31-reload-and-restart.ts), including 14-chat.ts, 21-late-join.ts, 22/23-subagent-*.ts and 26-coding-agent.ts.

cd ~/work
git clone https://github.com/earendil-works/pi
# library for your own project:
mkdir pim && cd pim && npm init -y
npm install @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai @earendil-works/chord

The post's demos run from a checkout of the v1.0.0 tag:

cd ~/work/pi && git checkout v1.0.0
npm install && npm run build
node packages/coding-agent/src/experimental/durable/main.ts
node packages/coding-agent/src/experimental/vacation/main.ts

INFERRED On current main, packages/coding-agent/src/experimental/ no longer contains these demos, so use the v1.0.0 tag. I haven't tested whether npm run build of the full monorepo completes in Termux. Native modules may need pkg install python make clang.

Stage 3: Have Pi build your own "pim" on the phone FROM HIS POSTSINFERRED prompt

He built it "directly in pi on my phone": Pi Durable as the core, plus "the control plane and ui on top of it". He described it as a server on the phone that you open in a browser ("this spins up a server on my phone, and i can test in the browser"), with the tablet as a client ("agents run on my phone, tablet connects to it"). For the general approach he recommends: "pi durable as the core, build everything around it including nice UI in an afternoon", and "if you give your agent the pi durable examples … it can likely figure it out".

A starter prompt for Pi, inside ~/work/pim (my wording, not his):

Read ../pi/packages/durable/README.md and ../pi/packages/durable/test/examples/
(especially 06-harness, 14-chat, 17-coding-tools, 21-late-join, 22/23-subagent, 26-coding-agent).
Build a small Node server that:
- opens a Pi Durable Harness on SQLite storage (./agent.sqlite) with CodingTools and NodeExecutionEnv
- serves a mobile-friendly web chat UI on 0.0.0.0:8080 (list conversations, new / fork, stream answers,
  show tool output, steer a running agent, show subagents)
- uses conversation.watch()/viewState() so several browsers can join the same conversation
- calls harness.resume() on start so interrupted runs continue after a crash.
Keep it minimal; it must run in Termux on Android.

Then grow it the way he did, one feature at a time: artifacts → paged transcript history → a tool to message other agents/subagents → a cwd file browser and git viewer → inline review comments sent back to the agent.

node server.js        # or whatever pi generated
# phone browser: http://localhost:8080 ; tablet on same Wi-Fi: http://<phone-ip>:8080

INFERRED He didn't say how his other devices reach the phone. On the same Wi-Fi the phone's LAN IP works. Outside the house you'd need something like Tailscale. Don't expose the port publicly without authentication.

Stage 4: Keep it alive when the screen is locked FROM HIS POSTSINFERRED commands

He said: "keeps working, termux process is forcibly kept alive via a setting." He didn't name the setting. The usual options are:

termux-wake-lock      # or "Acquire wakelock" in the Termux notification

Also: Android Settings → Apps → Termux → Battery → Unrestricted (turn off battery optimisation). Even if Android does kill it, Pi Durable resumes interrupted tasks from SQLite after a restart DOC, so treat the restart as normal.

Stage 5 (optional): Brain on the phone, hands on a server FROM HIS POSTSDOCINFERRED

"the little agent on the phone can change its execution environment from the phone to e.g. my hetzner in the same session. it's brain stays on my phone." Pi Durable builds a fresh execution environment for each tool call through your env function DOC. The Pi repo also contains packages/env ("pi-env"), which runs tools on a remote host over a reused SSH connection. A community video demoed it with pi-durable (@verysmallwoods, reposted by Mario).

INFERRED Ask Pi to wire packages/env's SSH/remote environment into your harness's env function, keyed per conversation. Set up an SSH key from Termux (pkg install openssh; ssh-keygen; ssh-copy-id user@server).

Stage 6 (advanced): Native Android app without Termux FROM HIS POSTS

"android native app achieved, no more termux needed" (4 Oct). "i just ripped the parts from termux i need and built a bespoke simple android app." His advice for doing the same: "just point your agent at termux repo and say: i just need the usrrland emu and the background process stuff so my shit doesn't die."

@arisonxdaniel built a similar "pi-mobile" with "full native android shell + toybox NO TERMUX" and said he would host the repo. I found no link yet, so check his profile.

INFERRED This means building an APK (Android SDK/Gradle) that bundles Node and a userland and runs the server as a foreground service. Only attempt it once Stage 3 works.

Pitfalls

  • Mario's app isn't available. Expect to build your own. The Pi Durable API is marked experimental and may change.
  • Use Termux from F-Droid or GitHub. The Play Store build is deprecated DOC.
  • Android kills background processes. Use a wake lock and unrestricted battery (Stage 4).
  • bash isn't replay-safe: "it can resume mid tool call, if the tool is durable itself (aka replay safe). bash is not. subagents are." After a crash, an interrupted bash call is reported to the model, not rerun FROM HIS POSTS.
  • Don't type to your agent while driving. He admitted one typo came from exactly that.
  • Exposing the phone's server outside your LAN without authentication gives strangers a shell on your phone.
  • Only the LLM is in the cloud, so API costs still apply. Pick a cheap model for subagents.
  • No AI SDK/UI adapters are planned ("an agent will be able to cobble those together from what pi-durable emits") FROM HIS POSTS. Hibernation and telemetry improvements were announced for the week of 19 Oct.
